title: Two Pointers & Sliding Window
relevance: High (appears constantly in modern OAs and interviews, especially FAANG).
company_notes: Longest continuous server uptime / longest continuous subarray → sliding window for a longest segment under a sum/condition. Maximum items within a budget / subarray sum equals K → shrink left when the sum exceeds the budget (array strictly positive). Target sum from two databases/lists → opposite-ends or two-array pointers on sorted inputs. Minimum window to cover all required skills (Amazon/Google) → Minimum Window Substring reskin.

phases.goal: Establish that the problem is two pointers or sliding window: a contiguous segment or pair under a monotone condition.

must_hit.point: The core idea is maintaining a valid segment with two index pointers L and R, exploiting monotonicity of a property (e.g., as the segment grows, its sum only increases).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names L/R on a contiguous segment and cites a monotone property such as growing sum.

must_hit.point: Recognize it when you need a contiguous subarray, substring, or pair satisfying a condition, or when the ask is longest, shortest, or number of valid contiguous sequences.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to contiguous subarray/substring/pair or longest/shortest/count of valid contiguous sequences.

must_hit.point: OA disguises include longest continuous server uptime / longest continuous subarray, maximum items within a budget / subarray sum equals K, target sum from two lists, and minimum window to cover all required skills.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the wording to one of those four OA/interview disguises from the Where-it-appears section.

probes: What in the statement says this is a contiguous L/R segment (or sorted pair) rather than a nested brute scan?
Is the ask longest, shortest, count of valid contiguous sequences, or a pair/target from two lists—and which disguise does that match?

hints.1: Ask whether the answer lives in a contiguous segment or a pair of indices under a monotone condition.
hints.2: Look for longest/shortest/number-of contiguous sequences, or a target pair from sorted inputs.
hints.3: Name L/R + monotonicity, and map to uptime/budget-sum, two-list target sum, or skills-cover minimum window.

phases.goal: Choose the right pointer pattern—sliding window, opposite ends, or two arrays—and the counting/state rule before coding.

must_hit.point: Sliding window: expand with R and shrink by advancing L only when constraints are violated, never resetting L, so the scan stays linear.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes expand-R / shrink-L with L moving only forward under the constraint.

must_hit.point: Opposite ends pointers: on a sorted array set L = 0 and R = N - 1 to find pairs (Two Sum II pattern).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States L and R at opposite ends of a sorted array moving toward a target pair.

must_hit.point: Two pointers on two arrays: traverse A and B simultaneously without nested loops (e.g., merging sorted arrays or finding the closest pair).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says advance pointers across two sequences in one coordinated pass, not nested loops.

must_hit.point: Counting subarrays: when window [L, R] is valid, it adds R - L + 1 valid subarrays ending at R.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the R - L + 1 contribution for each valid right endpoint R.

probes: Which pattern fits—sliding window, opposite ends on sorted input, or two-array pointers—and why?
If the problem asks for a count of valid contiguous subarrays, what do you add when [L, R] is valid?

hints.1: Classify as window on one array, opposite ends on sorted, or coordinated pointers on two arrays.
hints.2: Window: expand R and advance L only when invalid; pairs: L = 0, R = N - 1; two arrays: one pass, no nesting.
hints.3: For counts, when [L, R] is valid add R - L + 1 subarrays ending at R.

phases.goal: Code the concrete expand/shrink loop, opposite-ends or two-array walk, and O(1) window state structures.

must_hit.point: The O(N) sliding window template: a for loop for R expanding the window, and a while loop inside advancing L to shrink when constraints are violated.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes or describes for-R expand plus inner while advancing L on violation.

must_hit.point: Opposite ends implementation: L = 0 and R = N - 1 on sorted arrays to find pairs (Two Sum II).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Initializes opposite ends and moves L/R based on how the pair sum compares to the target.

must_hit.point: Monotonic queue extension: maintain a std::deque to retrieve the sliding maximum/minimum of a window in O(1) amortized time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses a deque of indices/values to answer window max/min as the window slides.

must_hit.point: Frequency map states: use an array or std::unordered_map plus an integer distinct_count so each pointer move updates conditions in O(1), avoiding recalculation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Increments/decrements freq and distinct_count on L/R moves instead of rescanning the window.

probes: Walk through the for-R / while-L sliding window template on a longest-window-with-sum constraint.
How do you keep window max/min or distinctness updated in O(1) per pointer move?

hints.1: Start from expand R; say when and how L advances.
hints.2: Template: for R, while invalid advance L; pairs: L = 0, R = N - 1; state via deque or freq + distinct_count.
hints.3: Name std::deque for sliding max/min and freq/distinct_count updates that avoid full recalculation.

phases.goal: Justify the linear scan and O(1) per-move state updates versus nested or rescanning approaches.

must_hit.point: By not resetting L, nested loops O(N^2) optimize down to a linear O(N) scan.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts resetting L (quadratic nested loops) with monotone L advances yielding O(N).

must_hit.point: A std::deque for sliding maximum/minimum answers each query in O(1) amortized time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States amortized O(1) window max/min via the monotonic deque.

must_hit.point: Frequency map plus distinct_count tracks conditions in O(1) time per pointer movement, avoiding recalculation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Claims O(1) work per L or R step via incremental freq/distinct updates.

probes: Why is the sliding-window scan O(N) rather than O(N^2)?
What makes each pointer move O(1) when you need max/min or distinctness in the window?

hints.1: Ask whether L ever moves backward or restarts from the left.
hints.2: Each index enters and leaves the window at most once → O(N); keep state incremental.
hints.3: Cite O(N^2)→O(N) by not resetting L, deque max/min in O(1) amortized, and freq/distinct_count O(1) per move.

phases.goal: Catch resetting L, illegal sum-window shrinks, bad counting, and full-window recalculation.

must_hit.point: Resetting L for each R (or otherwise re-scanning from scratch) reintroduces nested O(N^2) behavior and loses the linear scan.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses restarting L at 0 for every R and insists L only advances.

must_hit.point: For budget / subarray-sum shrink-from-left windows, shrinking when the sum exceeds the constraint is valid only if the array is strictly positive.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out the strictly-positive requirement before using classic sum-exceeds shrink.

must_hit.point: When counting valid contiguous subarrays, forgetting that a valid [L, R] contributes R - L + 1 endings at R undercounts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses R - L + 1 per valid R rather than counting only the full window once.

must_hit.point: Rescanning the whole window to recompute frequencies or distinctness instead of updating on each pointer move wastes the O(1)-per-move design.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Updates freq/distinct_count on L/R moves rather than rebuilding from the segment.

probes: What goes wrong if you reset L every time R advances?
When is shrink-on-sum-exceeds unsafe, and how do you count all valid subarrays ending at R?

hints.1: Check whether L only moves forward and whether sums are monotone.
hints.2: No L reset; sum-shrink needs a strictly positive array; counts add R - L + 1.
hints.3: Also keep freq/distinct_count incremental—do not rescan the window each step.

tradeoffs.topic: Nested O(N^2) scan vs O(N) two pointers
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Resetting L for each R is nested O(N^2); advancing L only forward under monotonicity yields a linear O(N) scan.

tradeoffs.topic: Opposite-ends pair search vs sliding window on a contiguous segment
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Opposite ends (L = 0, R = N - 1 on sorted input) finds pairs (Two Sum II); sliding window maintains a contiguous L..R segment for longest/shortest/count under a constraint.

tradeoffs.topic: Two-array pointers vs nested loops over A and B
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Traverse A and B simultaneously with two pointers (merge / closest pair style) instead of nested loops over both arrays.

tradeoffs.topic: Rescanning window state vs frequency map + distinct_count
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prefer an array or std::unordered_map plus distinct_count updated in O(1) per pointer move over recalculating the whole window.

tradeoffs.topic: Rescanning for window max/min vs monotonic deque
tradeoffs.strong_answer: A std::deque keeps sliding maximum/minimum in O(1) amortized time as the window moves (Sliding Window Maximum pattern).

gotchas.trap: Resetting L for every new R (nested loops).
gotchas.correction: Advance L only when the constraint is violated so each index moves at most once and the scan is O(N).

gotchas.trap: Using shrink-when-sum-exceeds on an array that is not strictly positive.
gotchas.correction: Classic left-shrink for budget / subarray sum needs a strictly positive array so growing/shrinking the window is monotone in sum.

gotchas.trap: Counting only one subarray per valid window instead of all endings at R.
gotchas.correction: When [L, R] is valid, add R - L + 1 valid subarrays ending at R.

gotchas.trap: Recomputing frequencies or distinctness by scanning the whole window after each move.
gotchas.correction: Maintain freq (array or std::unordered_map) and distinct_count so each pointer movement updates state in O(1).

gotchas.trap: Recomputing the window maximum/minimum by scanning the segment each time.
gotchas.correction: Maintain a std::deque for sliding max/min in O(1) amortized time.
